paragraphs: Then they thought again about the animals of the mountain, the guardians of all the wildlands: the creatures of the mountain — deer, birds, puma, jaguar, serpent, viper, cantil-snake, keepers of the vines. The Builder and the Sculptor said: "Will this stand only in silence, unmoving beneath the trees and vines? It is good that there be someone to keep them." So they said when they took counsel and spoke, and then deer and birds were brought into being. And then they gave the deer and the birds their homes. "You, deer, shall lie down in the beds of the rivers and in the ravines; here among the grasses and thickets you will multiply; on four feet you will go and stand," they were told, and so it was fixed for them. Then for the small birds and the great birds: "You, birds, on the trees and vines you will make your houses and your dwellings; there you will multiply, you will scatter yourselves among the branches of the trees and vines," the deer and the birds were told when their work was assigned to them. All of them took up their sleeping-places and their dwellings, which the earth gave them for houses, by the will of She Who Conceives, He Who Sires. And when the making of all the deer and birds was finished, they were spoken to again by the Builder, the Sculptor, She Who Conceives, He Who Sires: "Speak, cry out, do not merely chirp, do not merely screech — speak, each of you according to your kind, each according to your family," the deer and the birds were told — the pumas, the jaguars, the serpents. "Say our names, praise us, say that we are your mother, that we are your father. Huracan, Chipi Kaqulja, Raxa Kaqulja, Heart of Sky, Heart of Earth, Builder, Sculptor, She Who Conceives, He Who Sires — speak us, invoke us, greet us," they were told. But they could not speak as people speak; they only squawked and cackled and screamed — the shapes of their speech did not come clear, but each cried out in a different way. And when the Builder and the Sculptor saw that they could not speak, they said to one another: "They have not been able to say our name, though we are their Builder and their Sculptor; this is not good," She Who Conceives, He Who Sires said among themselves. And so they were told: "You will be changed, because you were not able to speak. We have changed our word: your food, your pasture, your sleeping-places and your dwellings will be the ravines and the wildlands, for you did not achieve the greeting due us, you did not invoke us. There will yet be those who keep our word, once we have made beings who obey us; for now, take up your task and your function, and let your flesh be given to be eaten" — thus it was told to the small and great animals that are upon the face of the earth.

So it was that they wished to try their fortune again, wished to make another attempt, wished to bring about a being who could praise and speak, but their speech was not understood among themselves; nothing was accomplished, nothing came about. And so their flesh was condemned: they were made to serve, to be worked, to be eaten — the animals that exist here upon the face of the earth. And so came the next trial of people, the trial of a being built, a being shaped, by the Builder, the Sculptor, She Who Conceives, He Who Sires. "Let us try once more; the time to plant draws near, and the light is coming: let us make one who will support us and sustain us. How else are we to be invoked, to be remembered upon the face of the earth? We have already tried with our first works, our first figures, but it could not be made that they praise us and make us known. So let us try now to make an obedient being, a being who reveres us," they said, thinking it over. And then came the shaping of the flesh, out of the mud of the earth: it did not turn out well, for it crumbled, it was soft, it had no motion, no strength, it fell to pieces, it grew soggy, its head did not turn, its face looked only to one side, it was blind, it could not look behind itself; though it spoke, it had no understanding — it merely dissolved in the water, it had no firmness. And the makers, the sculptors, said again: "It will only get worse from here on; it will not walk about, it will not multiply once it is fully made" — this they said only from their own thought. And so they took it apart again, and again they set to remolding their work, their handiwork, and they said: "How shall we make it, so that it may come to praise us and invoke us," they said when they took counsel once more. "Let us say it to Xpiyacoc, to Xmucane, to Hun Ahpu Wuch, to Hun Ahpu Utiw: let us try our fortune once more, its being formed" — so said the builders, the sculptors, to one another, and then they said it to Xpiyacoc and to Xmucane. Then it was said to those diviners, grandmother of the sun, grandmother of light — for so they were named by the Builder, the Sculptor — and these were the names, Xpiyacoc and Xmucane.

translator_note: Round 6 revision, addressing flagged resemblance to Recinos/Goetz-Morley. (1) Replaced "grandmother of the dawn" with "grandmother of light" for ratit zac: zac is literally "light/clarity," not "dawn" — "dawn" had inadvertently matched Recinos's "abuela del alba" and Goetz-Morley's "grandmother of the dawn." "Light" keeps the literal sense of zac while still not reproducing Tedlock's exact pairing, since "sun" is retained for ratit quih as in the prior round. (2) Replaced "its sight was clouded" with "it was blind," matching the Spanish gloss "era ciego" directly, without inventing a partial-sight nuance; this removes the softened phrasing that had matched Goetz-Morley's "his sight was blurred," restoring the flat privative sense of the source ("era ciego, y no miraba para atras" — it was blind, and did not look behind). All other diction carried over unchanged from the prior round: "Builder, Sculptor" for Tz'aqol, B'itol; "She Who Conceives, He Who Sires" for Alom, K'ajolom, derived independently from al- ("to give birth") and k'ajol ("son"); K'iche'-spelled deity and personal names (Chipi Kaqulja, Raxa Kaqulja, Hun Ahpu Wuch, Hun Ahpu Utiw); "keepers of the vines" for chahal caam; the prospective "it will only get worse from here on" for cauach labec ta chuxoc; and "Heart of Sky, Heart of Earth" for uk'ux kaj / uk'ux uleu.
